newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP slams Commission's air traffic control plans.
newsitem.headline: EP slams Commission's air traffic control plans.

text.p: Euro-MPs on Friday condemned as unsatisfactory the European Commission's plans for improving air traffic management and control within the European Union .

The European Parliament said the Commission's white paper, COM(96)57, glossed over the problem of the EU's fragmented air space, which has led to flight delays costing some two billion European currency units (Ecus) a year and to a rise in air accidents and near misses.
In a report drafted by Dutch Christian Democrat Petrus Cornelisson, the parliament demanded a strategic plan to bring in a single air traffic management and control system.
European airspace should be considered a common resource which had to be managed collectively by all 15 EU member states, Euro-MPs said.
They pointed out that civil airspace users had recommended that guidelines for managing European skies be set by a single body.
Each country or group of countries could then use these policies as the basis on which to run their own air traffic control services.
Contrary to what the Commission seemed to think, having a single, coordinated management system did not mean there would only be one service-provider for the whole of the EU, the report said.
